Shri Gulab Sohane, Advocate for the respondent No.2.
 ORDER Heard on I.A.No.21480/2024, an application for condonation of delay in filing the appeal.
On due consideration, I.A. is allowed.
Delay of 231 days in filing the appeal is, hereby, condoned.

This Miscellaneous Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is filed by the claimant/appellant, being aggrieved of the award dated 31.10.2023, passed by learned Sixth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur, in MACC No.1348/2022, on the ground that there is a disability certificate available on record as Ex.P/18, showing disability of the claimant to be 25%, but learned Tribunal for the purpose of computation of loss of earning capacity has only taken 8% functional disability.
2.

sentences.text:
Another ground which is taken by learned counsel for the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:12330 2 MA-7598-2024 appellant is that under the head of fracture, pain and sufferings, nutritious diet, attendant, his future treatment and transport, no amounts have been awarded by the learned Tribunal and, therefore, this appeal.

3. Shri Mohd. Riyaz, learned counsel for the appellant places reliance on a decision of a Coordinate Bench at Gwalior in M.A.No.205/2011 (Rajendra @ Sukha S/o Harjeet Singh Jatav Vs. Union of India and another), decided on 09.02.2014.

sentences.text: 4. Shri Gulab Sohane, learned counsel for the respondent No.2, supports the impugned award.
5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, it is evident that none of the doctors have been examined in support of the certificate.
Be that as it may be, the fact of the matter is that even aspect of functional disability has not been brought on record.

Therefore, it is evident that in the light of the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and another [(2011) 1 SCC 343] , where the ratio of the law is that in disability certificate extent of disability of a limb or part of the body cannot be assumed to be the extent of disability of whole body, though has been referred to by the Coordinate Bench at Gwalior, but has not discussed this aspect which is the ratio of the law of the land promulgated by the Hon'ble Apex Court.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12330 3 MA-7598-2024

entities.text: Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and another [(2011) 1 SCC 343]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, plea of enhancement of the percentage of disability from 8% to 25% merely on the basis of a certificate, is not made out and on that ground, appeal does not call for any interference.
6. As far as other heads are concerned, it is true that claimant suffered fracture of left hand wrist with a wound near the waist.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand), is admissible under the head of fracture/pain and sufferings.
7. Learned Tribunal has not awarded any compensation under the head of attendant.

Therefore, a sum of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand), is awarded under the head of attendant @ Rs.5,000/-
(Rupees Five Thousand), per month for a period of two months.

Similarly, another sum of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand), is awarded under the head of nutritious diet @ Rs.5,000/-
(Rupees Five Thousand), per month for a period of two months.

Tribunal has not awarded any amount under the head of transport, for which another sum of Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand),
is allowed.
Tribunal has not awarded any amount under the head of loss of income, for which another sum of Rs.16,000/- (Rupees Sixteen Thousand), is awarded for loss of earning for a period of two months.
Another sum of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand), is awarded under the head of future treatment, physiotherapy etc..

8. Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.76,000/-
(Rupees Seventy Six Thousand), which will be admissible in favour of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:12330 4 MA-7598-2024 the claimant.
This amount will carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of the Claim Petition till the date of actual payment.
9. Other terms and conditions of the award shall remain intact.
10. In above terms, appeal is disposed of.
(VIVEK AGARWAL) JUDGE A.Praj.
